source_text: Ostendi quidem in tertio libello primi operis mei, irrefutabiliter necesse esse dici etiam Christum reatum de Mariae carne traxisse, si crederetur naturale peccatum; eumque a te sub potestate diaboli collocari, qui affirmares ad ius diaboli hominum universam pertinere substantiam.
pass_a_gloss: I showed indeed in the third little book of my first work that it is irrefutably necessary that even Christ be said to have drawn guilt from Mary's flesh, if a natural sin were believed; and that he is placed by you under the power of the devil, you who would affirm that the whole substance of humans belongs to the devil's right.

lemmas.lexica: LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS opus; Blaise God's works vs devil's

pass_b_english: I showed in the third book of my first work that, if natural sin were believed, one would necessarily and irrefutably have to say that Christ too inherited guilt from Mary’s flesh. You place him under the devil’s power by asserting that the entire substance of human beings belongs to the devil’s jurisdiction.

choices.why: Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
